shippingNews.postTitle: BBC Philippines LNG Tanks Successfully Unloaded at Sturgeon Bay

stories.body: STURGEON BAY, WI – The 482-foot-long heavy lift vessel BBC Philippines departed Sturgeon Bay Monday for Burns Harbor after finishing unloading four huge Liquid Natural Gas (LNG) tanks. The tanks are for the new build 3794, a bunkering barge being built at Bay Shipbuilding that will be used to fuel ships at sea. Each thank had to be individually barged from the ship, anchored out in the bay, to the shipyard. Basic Marine’s tug Nickelena powered the barge with assistance from the smaller tug Krystal. shippingNews.postTitle: Iron Ore, Steel Shipments Decline at Great Lakes Ports Due in Part to Trump Tariffs

stories.body: Great Lakes ports are seeing declines in iron ore and steel shipments that are tied in part to the ongoing trade dispute between the U.S. and Canada. In August, President Donald Trump imposed 50 percent tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods, including alcohol, dairy products and motor vehicles. Canada responded on Sept. 8 with about $20 billion of its own retaliatory tariffs that include steel, agricultural equipment and pulp and paper products. LUDINGTON, MI – The Lake Michigan caferry Badger’s 2026 sailing season ended on Sunday, Oct. 11 when she docked for the winter at her Ludington, MI, home port. The Badger, operated by Lake Michigan Carferry, a part of Interlake Maritime Services, offers the largest cross-lake passenger service on the Great Lakes and an authentic steamship experience. The four-hour, 60-mile cruise takes passengers, autos, RVs, tour buses, motorcycles, bicycles, and commercial trucks across Lake Michigan between Ludington and Manitowoc, WI. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: Lake Superior remains situated between a 29.6 inch low over Wisconsin and a 30.2 inch high over Quebec. Ridging dominates over Lake Superior midweek as the low marches east and high pressure of 30.2 inches builds over the Dakotas by Wednesday afternoon. The high further builds to 30.3 inches over Lake Superior Wednesday night while a 29.9 inch low develops over Saskatchewan. By Thursday evening, this low weakens to 29.9 inches over northern Ontario as the high moves to New England, then the low rapidly deepens into Friday while tracking towards New England. Meanwhile, 30.6 inch high pressure expands across the Plains for Friday. Pressure increases rapidly over the Upper Great Lakes Friday afternoon into Saturday, reaching 30.4 inches by Saturday morning, then decreasing to 30.0 inches by Saturday night as the high collapses southeast.

West to northwest winds are expected today, remaining breezy as low pressure departs east. Light north winds expected tonight night, with isolated thunderstorms possible across far southern portions of the lake. Northerly winds continue Wednesday as high pressure moves eastward over the northern half of the lake, then easterly into Wednesday night as high pressure moves eastward. Winds weaken into Thursday as low pressure moves east through the Mississippi Valley, then become northwesterly gales late Thursday night into Friday as low pressure moves into the eastern Great Lakes and intensifies. A few storm force gusts are possible Friday.

Low pressure, 29.60 inches, moves across northern lower Michigan this morning. Departure of this system will then facilitate the passage of a cold front tomorrow morning, bringing breezy northwest flow across northern Lake Huron.

Low pressure 29.80 inches passes north of the lake today dragging a cold front over Lake Erie this evening. The front will push south Wednesday morning before high pressure 30.10 inches briefly builds north of the lake Wednesday night and Thursday. A strong cold front will pass over the region Friday morning as low pressure 29.60 inches moves north of the lake. High pressure 30.40 inches builds in from the west Saturday.

A cold front will sweep southeast across the lower Great Lakes this afternoon. Behind the cold front, a ridge averaging 30.2 inches will build in from northern Ontario through Thursday. A low averaging 29.5 inches may move across the Great Lakes region Friday. There is uncertainty in the track of this low, with the potential of deepening as it crosses the region. A 30.5 inch high will build into the Great Lakes region this weekend.
